title: Rava of Parzakya
author: Aharon Hyman

paragraphs: Hyman considers him too to have taken a large part with Rav Ashi in arranging the Talmud, for he discusses matters with Rav Ashi, as in [Yevamot 59b](https://www.sefaria.org/Yevamot.59b.8) (where it reads “of Parkin,” erroneously, in Hyman’s judgment), [Ketubot 39b](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.39b.11), [Nazir 38b](https://www.sefaria.org/Nazir.38b.8) (where it reads Ravina, erroneously, in Hyman’s judgment), [Bava Kamma 36a](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Kamma.36a.2), [Bava Batra 4b](https://www.sefaria.org/Bava_Batra.4b.4) and [Zevachim 10b](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.10b.24) and 108 (compare [108a](https://www.sefaria.org/Zevachim.108a.2)).
We find in [Eruvin 3a](https://www.sefaria.org/Eruvin.3a.20) that he resolves Rabbah’s law, and Ravina resolved it differently.
He issued rulings, as in [Pesachim 76b](https://www.sefaria.org/Pesachim.76b.10): a certain fish that was roasted with meat — Rava of Parzakya forbade eating it with kutach.
We find Huna Mar son of Rava of Parzakya, as in [Ketubot 10a](https://www.sefaria.org/Ketubot.10a.13).[^3]

notes.text: The proposed emendations and claim of participating in arranging the Talmud remain Hyman’s. The supplied Zevachim 108 has no side; the invented a is removed. The fish-with-meat ruling and son Huna Mar remain separate statements.
The participation in arranging the Talmud and the proposed corrections of Parkin and Ravina are Hyman’s judgments; the supplied Zevachim 108 reference does not specify a side.

The consulted Yevamot gives Parzakya, and Nazir gives Ravina of Parzakya where Hyman prefers Rava. Zevachim 108a directly names Rava of Parzakya addressing Rav Ashi. The supplied Hebrew puts a period after the abbreviated number. Heilprin discusses the Nazir and Yevamot variants and cites further parallels. See [Heilprin’s corresponding entry](https://www.girsology.com/seder-hadorot.html?entry=3184&lang=en).
